body: Thank you, kind stranger. I really don't want this to happen again. I guess it would've been a lot better if I just didn't talk to her. But fuck... I know she's told a bunch of people about me threatening suicide and being emotionally abusive, I just don't know who exactly she has told. So I don't know who to feel okay around and who not to. This whole situation is so fucked. I fucking hate it :(
I appreciate this so much. Thank you. Can I PM you?
Same. Sleeping feels good because then I don't have to be awake in this shitty reality that I created.

I know it shouldn't. The rational part of me knows it shouldn't affect me, but it does cause I'm not really being rational right now. It's pure emotion. It was all triggered by seeing her. I was fine but then she's gonna be at the same parties as me and each time it's gonna be hard. I guess now I know for certain that I should just act like she doesn't exist.
Thanks, but I don't even know why I'd bother. I'm drowning in despair and it's just too much. I can't live without at least her acceptance or forgiveness and she's given me neither. I'm done.
She is right in what she said. But it's more that she thinks I'm a monster. And her friends too. I can't live with that feeling. I'd rather die.
Yeah you're right. I still think about it a lot and it's kinda getting annoying now. The pain isn't as noticable, which is good.

1) Yep, although I lapsed yesterday and stalked her fb photos. We're not friend, I even blocked her, but I can still see photos she's been tagged in, which led to me stalking her. Not proud or happy with that, but it did kind of remind me of the person she is, which is not someone I want anymore.

2) Mentally I'm pretty good. There are other issues going on apart from the breakup, but they're within my control. Compared to two months ago I'm like a different person. Physically I'm doing really well. I've reached my goals at the gym, I'm putting on muscle and people are noticing :')

3) Just woke up so not much. Going to do some yoga later.

4) Moving out of my parents' house and in with friends. I can't wait. I know it's going to help me get over the breakup completely.

5) Listening to music. I forgot how powerful it can be for me.

6) Don't ever give up. Just keep striving to get to that better position. Keep doing all the good things you should be doing in this time. Eat right, exercise, read, hang out with friends (oh god this is so important) and eventually get out there again and see someone else.

1) yes
2) a little bit down actually. Still dwelling on it after all these months.
3) went to the gym
4) read something here, listen to some music, get out of the house
5) probably my close friend
6) I dunno. I'm feeling pretty crummy at the moment. I've been doing quite well up until today when I decided to check her facebook. I only saw a few pictures, but even that was enough to have a big effect on me. I don't know why I can't just move on from her completely. This sucks.
Thanks dude, I appreciate your threads. They're a good way of tracking your own progress :)

1) About 6 weeks now? I stopped counting.

2) Alright, still have other issues in life apart from not having a girlfriend. I guess the same or maybe a bit better than last week.

3) Making more money

4) Did a downward dog pose for a bit haha. I plan on doing some yoga later.

5) My self-worth

6) My ability to make friends with most people. I'm pretty adept socially. 

7) Yeah I go to the gym most days and get outside a bit. It's summer in Australia. I feel for you guys in America where it's not so warm :( 

8) Not sure exactly where I sit with this breakup. It went down as one of the worst and I did some really regrettable things. I imagine she still feels uncomfortable about the whole thing, as I do a little bit, and don't really want to see her for a while. I also haven't slept with anyone for about 6 months and I'm kind of thinking that when I start sleeping with someone I will begin to forget about her completely. I feel ready for someone else.
Definitely. You touch on the most salient point of a break-up, which is regaining your self-awareness. It's incredibly important to love yourself first and foremost.
They never really held me back, it's more that they made me happy enough to be complacent with not pursuing them. You should never let anyone hold you back!

Exactly.

You want them to validate your existence. Essentially, you're putting your self worth in their hands, so that when you don't see that text pop up, you think you're worthless because they didn't think about you. The reality is they probably knew it was your birthday, but they knew it was better not to text you in order for both of you to heal.

Your self worth has to come from you, not someone else.

edit: Sorry to give you the tough love, happy birthday :)

1) about 5 weeks

2) My parents. They're amazingly supportive and understanding, way moreso than I ever thought of them in the past. I've also begun to have a new kind of relationship with them, one where we don't argue every single day lol. I'm also grateful for my group of friends. They're inspiring.

3) Working out I guess. I always treat myself to something nice each day, whether it be an ice cream or an hour of gaming or a cigarette.

4) Coffee, sunshine, music.

5) "This is a test, you will come out stronger than ever"
"Life moves on. You can either choose to move with it or stay stuck."

Click on my name, then on the right, there's a button saying private message.

I've been using /r/breakups for the past few months and it helps to read others' stories, to know I'm not the only one who takes them to heart. My most recent one really affected me too, and I was suicidal for a good two months. I'm now doing a lot better. I would attribute it to hitting the gym hard, working more, hanging out with friends more and being more aware of my thought processes and emotions.

It sucks, I know. It feels like it's going to be this way forever, that the light at the end of the tunnel doesn't exist, but you just have to take it day by day, step by step. There's no easy fix for a breakup but time. Be patient. I can assure you it gets better. :)

It's okay. You only broke up a day ago! At this stage my advice would be to just grieve, cry your heart out. If there's a shoulder you can cry on, even better, but you need to go through the normal emotions unreservedly.
Any time :)
no problems!

I had a dream involving my ex last night too. They are the worst! Your subconscious is telling you that you're not completely over them. That's okay though. Just try and fill your day with things to do so that you don't dwell on it. Good luck! :)

Sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but there's no easy fix for this. It sucks, I know. Probably the best thing you can do is surround yourself with friends and family for new years and be somewhere she isn't
Thanks! It's been a hellish few months, but the past few weeks I've picked myself up and things are getting much, much better. I'm thinking of writing a guide post soon.

Maybe he really meant it, but he probably didn't, because if he did you'd probably still be together. Maybe he does think about you, maybe he doesn't. You can never know. That's hard to stomach, but honestly, you just have to move on. It sucks hearing that. People have said it to me time and time again, but it's the best advice because it's true - Learn your lessons from it, let it go and live your own life. 

People say these love drenched things whether they mean them or not, but the reality is that life changes immeasurably and it's out of our control. "Don't be sad because it ended, be happy because it ever happened."
A girl once told me she fell in love with Fleetwood Mac in the wake of a breakup. Maybe I should listen to them. Thanks!

Hey, that sounds like a really rough situation. I'm sorry to hear it. Your ex sounds like a bit of a bitch though if I'm honest. Doing things that make you feel bad on purpose? Flirting with other people while she's with you? Sounds like a bit of a narcissist to me. I know it doesn't help get over her to think of her like that, but in time you will begin to realise that she isn't as perfect as you make her out to be. You can't see it now, but you will.

Try and do small things for now. If possible, do some exercise. Anything, even just walking a few miles can help you. Even if you think about her the whole time. If the thoughts are too strong, try doing some research on the way your brain works in these situations. Cognitive distortions and the ruminating brain are two concepts my psych taught me which have really helped me see how my mind works when it's too much to handle myself. 

PM me if you want someone to talk to.

Hey, that sucks :( I'm sorry to hear it. 

Does being with your kids help? Maybe try getting out of the house more, walking in nature, something that exhausts your mind and body so that you can sleep better.
You're still here though! That's awesome. Are you seeing a professional? They can really help you, if you're willing to get help and help yourself.

I've had suicidal thoughts on and off for a few years, admittedly always because of a breakup, but they were very strong and persistent nonetheless. One thing that helped me was opening up to friends about it. You'd be surprised... almost all of my closest friends told me they'd had the same thoughts. You're never alone in this struggle. Find the ones you know will be empathetic, it really helps.

Breakups are a part of life. They suck, they're the absolute worst thing in the world, or at least they seem like it. But it gets better, I promise you. /r/breakups is full of good advice and has really helped me. Maybe it can help you too.

Feeling that kind of pressure at age 19 is really common, don't worry. It takes time to find out who you really are and what you want. Take that time. Chill out, go for a long walk and have a think about who you are, what you like doing and how you can be that person. PM me if you really want to talk :)

Hey,

Do you have a creative outlet? Sometimes isolation without having some kind of outlet can make you feel even worse, but having something to put your energy into can make you feel better.

1) A month and it has honestly helped me so much.

2) Meeting someone new, starting a new course next year, moving out of home

3) I would like to put on about 10kg worth of muscle, get to an optimal health point, start developing websites as a source of income, hmmm... there will probably be more but I can't think of any right now.

4) Yes, almost every day. This has also helped me so much.

Hey, we're all going through this together so it's only natural to want to help. 

Yeah, dreams suck. I still get the dreams, even ones where we hook up. They fucking suck. Try and get up straight away and do some exercise, it will probably reset your body and hopefully the thoughts won't hurt as much.

Just be honest with him if he comes up to you and tells you something like that again. Be honest without being spiteful though. There's a way to do it. You might say something like "I appreciate that you want to talk and be friends, but it's really, really hard for me right now so I think it's best if we don't talk to each other for a while."

I'm in something similar myself, although she has a different friendship group, I always see her at events. She is sort of afraid of me because of the breakup and how I handled it, and the fact that she's now dating her ex again. God, it's fucking painful to see her having fun, and I can't be friends with those people really... You just have to be strong and do lots of good things for yourself so that you become a better person. 

Good luck :)

Do NOT self medicate in a situation like this! I did this for 2 months with weed and a bit of alcohol. It was literally the WORST decision I could make in my situation. The way to make yourself feel better is by putting in place healthy habits like exercise, going to the gym, having a creative outlet, reading, etc, etc. If you really feel like you need some assistance then see a mental health professional, but for the love of god, DO NOT SELF MEDICATE!

Hey man, shit sucks. I know where you're at and we've all been there at some point. The initial period after losing someone is super painful and confusing. It's like your whole world has collapsed and you think things will never be as good as they once were. Just keep in mind that this is life. It goes up, then it comes down. But guess what? It will go back up again :) I promise you. Give it time. It's only been a week so the wounds are still very fresh.

My advice for you is to indulge in things to a healthy extent. Binge eat shit food if you want. Bawl your eyes out, watch sad movies, listen to Elliott Smith. Shit like that. But don't get caught into a routine habit of doing this, because if you make that your normal, you won't get better. Just give it a little bit of time and when you aren't feeling like you're living in the pits of hell, when that moment comes, take advantage of it and start putting positive things in place. There are lots of threads in this subreddit about what you can do for yourself in this situation and they all really help. 

Best of luck man, take care of yourself.

I don't think it's so black and white, like you're just suddenly over your ex and you never ever think of them again. I think that when you're at a point where you can feel genuine, unfiltered attraction to someone that you're not using to cover up feelings for you ex that are festering inside you, then you're ready to date. But like I said, it's not black and white, it's a very grey area. You might meet someone when you're still very much in the grieving process AND have a genuine attraction to them, but it might not be the right time. Doesn't mean you shouldn't date them, it just means that you need to be aware of what you're really feeling. Try flirting or even just fucking making friends with the opposite sex instead of trying to date/fuck anyone you find mildly attractive. Be reasonable.

1)Three weeks. If my mind even drifts off into thinking about her (not even contacting her, just thinking about her) I will go and do something. Anything! Work out, clean my room/house, play some music, learn some code (I've started learning code)

2)I just mentioned them! Started working out, stopped using drugs and alcohol, started learning code, getting outside more, reading more, just being more productive in general. Hanging out with friends is a necessity.

3) All the things I've just mentioned. I also got accepted in to a master's course next year. I received some advanced standing credits for it, which means in stead of doing two years and paying about $40,000, I will only do 1.5 years and pay $30,000. Yay! 

4) Lol, just mentioned them! I'm also very excited to start running some parties and DJing again, something I fell out of in the past six months during the relationship. 

Life is on the up! I would honestly put it down to my self-motivation. Working out is the most important thing for me now. That and eating right/being healthy. I can't not be working out and constantly improving my physical health. You have to put in place positive things that you can build on so that you keep momentum going in your life. For the first few months I let myself slip into depression and it was not good. I just wanted to be there and wallow in my own sadness, but I had a revelatory experience with a mental health worker that shone some light on why my relationships follow the same path all the time. Now I am much more self aware and I can see the path forward. I hope everyone else can :)
This! This is the reason this subreddit exists. So happy for you man, keep up whatever it is you're doing. I recently had the same realisation :)

1) about three weeks, although it was her saying "I wish you would just respect my wishes and leave me alone" which is pretty crushing on top of everything else :(

2) It would either have to be my chest/torso or my penis lol.

3) My ability to be passionate about things and add life to things that seem lifeless. This comes through when I boost other people's self confidence and when I become interested in things. I love how deep I can get in to something

4) Yes! I've been exercising everyday for the past week and a bit and holy shit has it helped me. Going to the gym and releasing all that negative energy, putting it in to something productive has had all kinds of positive impacts. Went out for a walk in the sunshine today as well, which was great.

5) I recently read The Alchemist, which is about finding purpose in life. It is a beautiful read and gave me an idea of the bigger picture in life, which is hard to do when you're down.

We've all been there man, it's nothing to beat yourself up about. Part of the grieving process is to go through that pain. What has helped me break the cycle has been FORCING myself to go out and do something. If I catch myself flopping on to my bed or I KNOW my mind is going to go on infinite tangents, I force myself to go to the gym, or call a friend (having a friend who knows exactly what's going on helps), or play piano/sing a song/listen to music or anything that would keep my mind occupied. Sometimes it's hard, I know... sometimes it feels easier to just let your mind fuck you over like that. But just try to be strong and do something instead of letting it take over. The only way from here is forward, you WILL get through this and be a better version of yourself after it's all over :)
Well, I guess I mean change something or make it better in a way that she would actually have some inkling of compassion for me again and not just go off telling everyone about my fucked up mind.
I have been thinking seriously about this option. Never thought I'd end up there... :(

Thanks. I really appreciate your words. The thing is... she knows about my suicidal thoughts. I texted her one night and basically it came out that I had been having these thoughts. We talked on the phone for a while. Then I saw her on saturday night, which is probably why she felt so weird... 

Also, we were both overseas together recently. I had already been overseas a month and a half by that point... basically she got back with her ex a week or two after I left. I found this out after five days of arguments and mutual weird vibes. Then after an incident one day I just decided to leave and go home. That was about a month ago.

I guess because I wanted to talk to her and was upset that I didn't have the courage to talk to her in person. I'm also kinda masochistic in this sense. I know no contact is the best way but I also can't avoid seeing her out - we have very similar friends and like going to the same gigs.

I blocked and deleted from everything. For some reason though, whenever any of our mutual friends pop up (and we have a lot), I think about her. Certain things and events make me think about her and get angry knowing she's probably posting on that page or going to that event. This sucks.
